question: What Eon, Eoff and Eoss does an independent VENDOR DEVICE MODEL predict at the campaign's real operating point, and does it agree with the maintained analytic model's 37.368 W overlap term?
why: The analytic Rust model attributes 37.4 W of the 45.5 W baseline to switching overlap, and the whole ranking depends on that term. A vendor SPICE device model is an independent implementation, so agreement or disagreement is real evidence. It is a model, not a measurement: report it as independent-model evidence, never as measured or hardware-qualified.

operating_point.note: clamped inductive double pulse; measure Eon at the turn-on current and Eoff at the turn-off current

focus: Capture the exact manufacturer SPICE model for the baseline device IPW65R045C7 (Infineon CoolMOS C7) and, if obtainable, IPZ60R040C7 and the retained board part STW65N65DM2AG. Build a clamped-inductive double-pulse testbench in ngspice: bus 400 V, gate drive 0->12 V through 9.7 ohm on / 5.3 ohm off, measure Eon at 11.9486 A and Eoff at 15.0071 A at 25 and 125 C, and Eoss at 400 V. Report per-event energy and the f-weighted average (Eon+Eoff)*f. Compare with the analytic 37.3682 W overlap and state the ratio. If a vendor model is encrypted, unavailable, or will not converge, say so with the exact failure and do not substitute the analytic model or a hand-built device model.
stop_rule: Do not tune the testbench until it agrees. A large disagreement is a finding, not a failure. Do not present a vendor model as measured data. If no usable vendor model can be captured, return UNKNOWN with the capture failures.
